messages.subject: Integer vector and matrix
parts:
Hi all,

I'm wondering if a vector of integers (and a matrix of integers) is possible ?

And, I also have a stupid question of algebra. How can I write the loops in vector matrix form ? (the first question is because I want D1 to be a matrix of integer)

data :: matrix[N,K] D1;
parameter :: vector[K] a;
parameter :: vector[N] d1;
transformed parameter :: matrix[N,K] phi1;

    for (i in 1:N1){
        for (j in 1:K){
            phi1[i,j] <- (D1[i,j]*a[j]) / d1[i];
        } 
    }

Thank you
Leon

On Oct 16, 2014 5:12 AM, "Leon-Alph" <leon.cor...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi all,
>
> I'm wondering if a vector of integers (and a matrix of integers) is possible ?

You can have an array of int and a multi-dimensional array of int. The vector and matrix types are of type real.

Examples:
int a[2];
int b[3,4];

>
> And, I also have a stupid question of algebra. How can I write the loops in vector matrix form ? (the first question is because I want D1 to be a matrix of integer)

I'm having trouble understanding your question. Maybe you want to read your data as a matrix instead of int? That'll allow you to use matrix operations.

With that said, loops are not slow in Stan.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Integer vector and matrix
parts:
Is there a reason you can't declare D1 as a matrix of
reals? You can assign integer values to real variables.
All the code you sent does is multiply the integers by
reals, which is going to implicitly promote the integers
to reals before multiplying anyway.

data :: matrix[N,K] D1;
parameter :: vector[K] a;
parameter :: vector[N] d1;
transformed parameter :: matrix[N,K] phi1;

for (i in 1:N1){
for (j in 1:K){
phi1[i,j] <- (D1[i,j]*a[j]) / d1[i];
}
}

As to the matrix issue, you're not doing matrix algebra
here, you're doing elementwise operations. You could remove
one loop and use the elementwise product operator ".*":

phi[i] <- (D[i] .* a) / d1[i]

But I don't see any way to remove both loops.

And doing it with ".*" won't be any faster because there's no
savings to be had in eliminating shared computation or storage
for derivatives, which are all compltely independent in
elementwise products..

- Bob
